TV is sort of like caffeine (another thing I gave up - though that one wasn't by choice, but required by my doctors) in that you cannot imagine yourself living without it and wouldn't want to. And the first few months of abstinence are genuinely very difficult. But eventually it gets easier, and then it gets completely easy, and then you actually feel as good or better than before. And once you finally become accustomed to it, you can't imagine going back to the old way.  [reply](reply?id=50208499&goto=item%3Fid%3D50205934%2350208499) | | | |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  |  | [bob1029](user?id=bob1029) [6 minutes ago](item?id=50208563)  | [parent](#50208499) | [next](#50208596) [[–]](javascript:void(0))   I haven't had a functional TV in my home for over 5 years now. I will sometimes watch shows on my laptop but that's about it. In place of a TV I have a high res audio transport and speakers that are used for music. Spotify isn't exactly a saint but it would be challenging for them to do what Disney is doing without losing all their customers.  [reply](reply?id=50208563&goto=item%3Fid%3D50205934%2350208563) | | | |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  |  | [awjlogan](user?id=awjlogan) [3 minutes ago](item?id=50208596)  | [parent](#50208499) | [prev](#50208563) | [next](#50208574) [[–]](javascript:void(0))   Another benefit is you don’t have a permanent black hole on the wall. You no longer have to force the room layout to focus on that space.  [reply](reply?id=50208596&goto=item%3Fid%3D50205934%2350208596) | | | |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  |  | [jerf](user?id=jerf) [5 minutes ago](item?id=50208574)  | [prev](#50208499) | [next](#50208634) [[–]](javascript:void(0))   From this point on, every year "physical media & a Jellyfin install" is going to be more sensible. Assuming you even care about legality, of course. Yeah, it's harder. But you can get a lot of "harder" things done in the amount of time you otherwise spend watching ads, after all. Because to me one of the worst things about ads is they're stealing dollars from me to make cents, if not fractions of a cent. This makes them on the dumb end of the bandit classification by the Basic Laws of Human Stupidity metric: [https://harmful.cat-v.org/people/basic-laws-of-human-stupidi...](https://harmful.cat-v.org/people/basic-laws-of-human-stupidity/) It's so *dumb*. And as long as we keep letting them give us an option to buy out the ads, but then they get to stick ads on that option anyhow, we can never get our way out of ads on these things. I don't mind buying them out because they make so little money anyhow but by simple game theory "buy out ads + put ads on anyhow" is always > "buy out ads". You need to cancel if they do this to you. I can't, because I don't have a Disney+ subscription. But you really need to. You need to turn the option into either "let us buy out the ads" or "lose the subscription" for them.  [reply](reply?id=50208574&goto=item%3Fid%3D50205934%2350208574) | | | |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  |  | [baq](user?id=baq) [0 minutes ago](item?id=50208634)  | [prev](#50208574) | [next](#50208191) [[–]](javascript:void(0))   I’ll cancel the moment I see the first ad. I’m likely not alone, but under no illusion that there are a lot of people like me, either.  [reply](reply?id=50208634&goto=item%3Fid%3D50205934%2350208634) | | | |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  |  | [thisislife2](user?id=thisislife2) [35 minutes ago](item?id=50208191)  | [prev](#50208634) | [next](#50207864) [[–]](javascript:void(0))   This is what happens when you don't have *consumer rights* protection. E.g. *Paid for ad-free OTT viewing but commercials ‘appeared after a month’, man wins Rs 9,500* ( [https://indianexpress.com/article/legal-news/paid-ad-free-ot...](https://indianexpress.com/article/legal-news/paid-ad-free-ott-viewing-commercials-after-month-man-wins-rs-9500-10927880/) ): > Calling it a deficiency in service, the Hyderabad consumer commission ordered an OTT platform to refund Rs 1,499 and pay compensation to a subscriber after it introduced advertisements midway into his paid ad-free subscription.  [reply](reply?id=50208191&goto=item%3Fid%3D50205934%2350208191) | | | |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  |  | [tkdb](user?id=tkdb) [1 minute ago](item?id=50208624)  | [parent](#50208191) | [next](#50208409) [[–]](javascript:void(0))   I'm not sure consumer rights protections would deliver better experiences. Government is predictably slow, inefficient, and does just about everything at a service level that is only accepted because there is no other choice. We are seeing an increasingly exaggerated cycle that goes like this: 1. Innovation takes huge investment to launch 2. Early adopters enjoy amazing new product(s) while companies bear losses 3. Companies eventually must face debt so quality of products decrease and price increases OpenAI and Anthropic have perhaps set the record for going from 1 to 2 in the biggest (financially) and fastest manner ever, and we are all hurtling towards step 3 with a possible too-big-to-fail scenario. Back to Disney Plus: I don't have a sagely answer. Free markets do sometimes need government to curb monopoly power, and Disney is certainly has a sort of monopolistic power due to their huge portfolio of franchises and content.  [reply](reply?id=50208624&goto=item%3Fid%3D50205934%2350208624) | | | |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  |  | [an0malous](user?id=an0malous) [18 minutes ago](item?id=50208409)  | [parent](#50208191) | [prev](#50208624) | [next](#50207864) [[–]](javascript:void(0))   Well, if you want the root cause: this is what happens when your society is predicated on perpetual growth. Everything would collapse if we just left good things alone, so instead we’re stuck either innovating and creating new good things or squeezing the juice out of what already exists.  [reply](reply?id=50208409&goto=item%3Fid%3D50205934%2350208409) | | | |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  |  | [izacus](user?id=izacus) [5 minutes ago](item?id=50208576)  | [root](#50208191) | [parent](#50208409) | [next](#50207864) [[–]](javascript:void(0))   This has nothing with perpetual growth and everything with training your population to defend these practices with "oh, they're just companies, don't use it if you don't like it!" instead of fighting back.  [reply](reply?id=50208576&goto=item%3Fid%3D50205934%2350208576) | | | |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  |  | [j-kent](user?id=j-kent) [1 hour ago](item?id=50207864)  | [prev](#50208191) | [next](#50208550) [[–]](javascript:void(0))   In the end, it all leads to advertising. This is just the basic business model in the US/World right now. Get enough eyeballs on your product, whether it's TV, social media, AI, the ditch on the side of the highway; then monetize it with ads. I don't understand why at this point anyone is surprised that a company like Disney would put ads every possible place, even their highest tier of streaming. "But I specifically chose the highest option so I wouldn't see ads!" well, now you have the option to pay the highest tier to see less ads. For now. By paying for the highest tier, Disney knows you are a higher quality consumer with the most disposable income of all the users on that platform; that's exactly the users Disney can charge the most for advertising spend. From an exec's standpoint, why wouldn't you? sure, they'll lose some paying customers, but will probably make more in the short term at least, which is all that matters.  [reply](reply?id=50207864&goto=item%3Fid%3D50205934%2350207864) | | | |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  |  | [LaurensBER](user?id=LaurensBER) [7 minutes ago](item?id=50208550)  | [prev](#50207864) | [next](#50208542) [[–]](javascript:void(0))   Given how good illegal alternatives like Stremio are this seems like a very dangerous game to play. You can squeeze customers quite a bit but once they go back to pirating it's incredible hard to get them to subscribe again.  [reply](reply?id=50208550&goto=item%3Fid%3D50205934%2350208550) | | | |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  |  | [HelloMcFly](user?id=HelloMcFly) [7 minutes ago](item?id=50208542)  | [prev](#50208550) | [next](#50208487) [[–]](javascript:void(0))   I just want a company to tell me truly what it is worth to them from me to not show me ads. Maybe the cost is truly so much higher than I expect that I wouldn't pay it, but for fuck's sake give me the option! Is it $15/month extra instead of $5? $30/month extra? Somewhere, that line exists where the company would financially benefit, I just wish they'd actually define it. When I was getting married, I engaged a baker to make pies for our wedding. Two weeks before the wedding they cancelled, saying very apologetically they had not catered many weddings with only pies and couldn't do it at the price they quoted. I had to practically *beg* them to just give me a price that was profitable for them (20% higher, in the end), and then let me decide. This feels just like that.  [reply](reply?id=50208542&goto=item%3Fid%3D50205934%2350208542) | | | |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  |  | [mosura](user?id=mosura) [4 minutes ago](item?id=50208581)  | [parent](#50208542) | [next](#50208487) [[–]](javascript:void(0))   If you would pay to remove ads you are more valuable, so they can charge more, in a never ending spiral. [reply](reply?id=50208150&goto=item%3Fid%3D50205934%2350208150) | | | |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  |  | [DiabloD3](user?id=DiabloD3) [55 minutes ago](item?id=50207938)  | [prev](#50208150) | [next](#50206533) [[–]](javascript:void(0))   Thats a weird way for Disney+ to go under.  [reply](reply?id=50207938&goto=item%3Fid%3D50205934%2350207938) | | | |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  |  | [damnesian](user?id=damnesian) [3 hours ago](item?id=50206533)  | [prev](#50207938) [[–]](javascript:void(0))   Corporatism is running rampant. It's almost a full-blown punishment model. Soon the entertainment platforms will be demanding a fee for NOT subscribing to their service.  [reply](reply?id=50206533&goto=item%3Fid%3D50205934%2350206533) | | | |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  |  | [kotaKat](user?id=kotaKat) [1 hour ago](item?id=50207798)  | [parent](#50206533) [[–]](javascript:void(0))   No, it IS a full-blown punishment model. Remember, everyone else is bundling this garbage with *their* service, too, so the price raises Disney does is an excuse that forces everyone downstream that bundles to raise prices too. I'm not even sure which Disney+ susbription I apparently am a part of at this point - my cable company provides it, my wireless provider provides it, hell, even shopping platforms are now shoving this crap into it as a 'perk'. I didn't want it in the first place but I'm forced to have it like a bundled set of cable channels I didn't want to subscribe to. ... dear God, it's just cable TV package cramming all over again just across every single service industry now.
